pr.title: GVN: Evaluate constants lazily.
pr.description:
GVN currently evaluates constants eagerly. This is not necessary. This PR makes constant evaluation on-demand to avoid unnecessary work.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR (rust-lang/rust#146869, "GVN: Evaluate constants lazily") is a pure performance refactor: it replaces eager Option<OpTy> population with a memoized tri-state lazy cache. The frozen analysis explicitly states this is "not a semantics-changing rewrite" and that the PR avoids unnecessary work rather than fixing wrong output. The only defects described are hypothetical implementation mistakes (conflating uncomputed `None` with failed `Some(None)`, bypassing the memoized wrapper, or forgetting failure caching), none of which alter the propagatable constant values for a valid acyclic value graph. A naive lazy cache would at worst miss an optimization or recompute, not change runtime semantics, and the patch adds no regression-test hunk with a changed expectation. Therefore there is no source-grounded original-vs-transformed function pair whose defined executions produce different observable values; constructing one would require manufacturing an unrelated semantic bug, which the task forbids.

analysis.summary: GVN changed constant evaluation from eager-at-insertion to lazy/memoized-on-demand. The reusable correctness knowledge is the tri-state cache invariant (uncomputed vs failed vs successful), the requirement that every consumer route through the memoized accessor, and pre-seeding opaque values as known failures while caching both successes and failures.
analysis.originalLogic: When GVN inserted a new value into `values`, it immediately called `self.eval_to_const(index)` and pushed the resulting `Option<OpTy<'tcx>>` into `evaluated`. Every later user, including recursive operand lookups inside `eval_to_const` itself, read `self.evaluated[f].as_ref()` directly. `new_opaque` pushed `None` because an opaque value can never be evaluated. Thus all evaluable values were computed eagerly even if GVN never needed their constant form.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation is the performance change itself: replacing eager `Option<OpTy>` population at insertion with a lazy `Option<Option<&OpTy>>` cache. This is not a semantics-changing rewrite and the PR describes it as avoiding unnecessary work, not fixing wrong output. The mistake to avoid when performing this transformation is a naive lazy cache that cannot distinguish three states: uncomputed, evaluation failed, and evaluation succeeded. After insertion becomes lazy (`self.evaluated.push(None)`), leaving any consumer with a raw `self.evaluated[i]` read, or recursing with the uncached `eval_to_const_inner`, would observe an uncomputed entry as if it were a failed evaluation and would lose or duplicate constant evaluation. Similarly, storing only a plain `Option` conflates uncomputed with failure, so failures and opaque values are repeatedly recomputed instead of being memoized as `Some(None)`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies optimized by GVN that contain values eligible for constant evaluation: constants, aggregates, unions, raw pointers, projections, address/deref values, discriminants, null ops (size/align/offset), unary and binary operations, and casts (integer/float, transmute/subtype, unsize/pointer coercions). The domain also includes values that cannot be constant-evaluated, such as `Value::Opaque`, addresses based on locals, and unsized values, plus shared subexpression DAGs where the same value index is queried more than once.
analysis.trigger: A value is inserted into GVN's `values` set, or an existing value is queried for its constant form during constant propagation or place/projection simplification.
preconditions: The lazy cache must be index-aligned with `values` and `rev_locals` (`debug_assert_eq!(index, _index)`).
Every newly inserted non-opaque value starts as uncomputed (`None`), while `new_opaque` starts as a cached failure (`Some(None)`).
Evaluation must occur before any result is read, and successful results must be arena-allocated so the cached `&'a OpTy` remains valid for the lifetime of `VnState`.
The value graph being evaluated must be acyclic/valid, and the existing coroutine layout-cycle avoidance must remain in place.
pitfalls: Conflating `None` (not computed yet) with `Some(None)` (computation failed); the source explicitly documents these three states.
Not pre-seeding `new_opaque` as `Some(None)`, causing known-unevaluable opaque values to be recomputed on every query.
Leaving any old direct read of `self.evaluated[...]` after insertion becomes lazy; all consumers, including recursive operand reads, must call `eval_to_const`.
Calling `eval_to_const_inner` recursively instead of the memoized `eval_to_const` wrapper, which bypasses both success and failure caching and can recompute shared subgraphs repeatedly.
Forgetting to cache the failed result `None` in the wrapper after `eval_to_const_inner` returns `None`.
Borrowing `evaluated` immutably across a call that needs `&mut self`; the `as_bits` closure must become `mut` because it now calls the mutable accessor.
Allocating the result in the arena after evaluation; storing a temporary local reference would not satisfy the `'a` lifetime.
analysis.testStrategy: Exercise each GVN constant-evaluation arm with small MIR-opt tests: aggregate construction, union field read, raw pointer with metadata, projection/index, address/deref, discriminant, unary/binary operations, and every cast kind (including transmute, unsize, and pointer coercions). Add a value that cannot be evaluated (opaque, local-address, or unsized) and query it more than once to check that failure is cached rather than mistaken for uncomputed. Add a shared subexpression DAG to verify memoization does not change results or repeatedly evaluate the same index. Since this PR only changes gvn.rs and supplies no regression-test hunk, compare GVN MIR output before and after the lazy refactor; the observable propagated constants should be identical for all supported values. The supplied patch itself shows no new test expectation, so do not claim a regression test was added or reproduced.
evidence: GVN currently evaluates constants eagerly. This is not necessary.
This PR makes constant evaluation on-demand to avoid unnecessary work.
